purpose: The v1 idempotent learning-event contract: what counts as the learner's first result on the reference Kochergina cohort, what the canonical effect of the event is, and why replaying it can never produce a second effect.

event.name: lesson_completed
event.actor: an entitled student (group membership + paid tariff key)
event.guard: StudentController::ensureLessonAccessible(): group visibility + tariff unlock, abort(403) otherwise
event.canonical_effect: exactly one lesson_user row per (user_id, lesson_id) with is_completed=1; replay updates the same row instead of inserting a second one (the pivot has no unique index, so the code guards: completedLessons()->exists() check, then updateExistingPivot vs attach)
event.telemetry: ActivityEvent LESSON_MARK_MASTERED is emitted only on the FIRST completion of a lesson; a replay click emits no second event
event.prana: lesson_complete award is idempotent per lesson_id (PranaService::award)

first_result_definition: the earliest lesson_user row with is_completed=1 for the user on the cohort's lessons; homework_submissions (statuses submitted/needs_revision/accepted) is the second, independent first-result signal
denominator_definitions_source: App\Services\Analytics\ActivationCompletionMetricsService (H3764) - activation anchor = StudentUnitEconomicsService::acquisitionAnchors() (first access-opening purchase); course denominator = course_user rows; group denominator = group_user rows; completion reads lesson_user.is_completed, never lesson_views.is_completed (dead on prod)

idempotent_replay.first_post: 302, one lesson_user row (is_completed=1), one LESSON_MARK_MASTERED event
idempotent_replay.second_post: 302 again, still exactly one lesson_user row, still exactly one LESSON_MARK_MASTERED event

rollback.action: revoke entitlement (cancel payment + detach group), then replay the event
rollback.expected: event is now rejected (403, content locked) while already-written progress history remains intact; no content or progress rows are deleted

prod_reference_cohort_434_gr61.note: timestamps verbatim from prod SELECT; the chain promise -> access -> first result is therefore observable end-to-end on this cohort
